subject: Reserved GPU commit: term/price-protection constructs
messages:
From: Tom Leland <tom@integro.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity request and initial profile

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking time. We're evaluating a reserved capacity commit to normalize inference costs for our customer-facing agents. High-level asks: 24-month and 36-month term options, an approximate monthly vGPU utilization profile (attached), and any price-protection constructs you can offer given market volatility in GPU costs.

Attached: Commit_Request.pdf (summary + initial volume curve). We can be flexible on phasing, but need clarity on what discount bands and protection you can offer.

Can we get a written offer by next Wednesday? Happy to jump on a call—Tom

--
Tom Leland
Head of Procurement, Integro AI
procurement@integro.ai
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Leland <tom@integro.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity request and initial profile

Tom — thanks for the details and the volume curve. Appreciate the flexibility. High-level options we can offer (draft):

Option A — 12/24/36 month fixed discount tiers
- 12m: 15% off list
- 24m: 28% off list
- 36m: 35% off list
Pros: predictable pricing; Cons: exposure to GPU-cost shocks.

Option B — 24/36 month with indexation cap (hybrid)
- Base discount (24m: 22%, 36m: 30%) + GPU market index pass-through above a 15% baseline
- Protection: monthly pass-through capped at +10% of monthly bill; if index > +25% for 3 consecutive months, parties can trigger a capacity rebaseline (reduce reserved quantity up to 20% or migrate to on-demand).

Option C — 36m top-tier discount with escrowed price-safety (requires finance/legal approval)
- 36m: up to 40% discount subject to an annual reconciliation and an escrow mechanism that shares incremental GPU cost increases. This option requires executive sign-off.

What we need from Integro to firm up numbers: month-by-month expected vGPU consumption (the attached summary helps but we need the detailed monthly curve), and whether you want a hard-cap or a rebaseline trigger.

I'll loop in finance and pricing for approval thresholds. If you want, we can sketch Option B with concrete formulas and a sample P&L. Proposed next step: quick sync early next week to align on the monthly profile, then I can send a formal offer.

Best,
Sean
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
sean@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity request and initial profile — quick pricing read

Marissa/Karthik — forwarding Integro's ask. TL;DR: they want 24/36m options and want some price-protection. I sketched three constructs (A: fixed tiers, B: hybrid indexation with cap + rebaseline trigger, C: aggressive discount with escrow).

Questions:
- Approval thresholds: what discount % can I commit to without VP sign-off? My read: >35% needs exec sign-off; >30% needs finance review. Please confirm.
- Are we comfortable with a rebaseline-trigger clause (reduce reserved quantity up to 20% if GPU index >25% for 3 months)?

Attachment: pricing-models.csv with a quick sensitivity run (assumes 30% baseline discount for 24m, 35% for 36m). I modeled 0/15/30% GPU cost shocks and EBITDA impact.

If we want Option C to be available I need an explicit cap or escrow mechanism from Finance/legal. Karthik, can you route a quick check?

Thanks — S

--
Sean Gallagher
Director, Solutions
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity request and initial profile — quick pricing read

Sean — reviewed. Approvals & quick guidance: 

1) Approval bands
- Up to 30% discount for multi-year committed deals: you can approve (Sales Ops delegated).
- 31%–38%: requires Sr. Director (Marissa) sign-off and Finance check.
- >38%: requires VP/Revenue Exec escalation and Legal to pre-approve any escrow mechanisms.

2) Rebaseline trigger
- We're ok with a capacity rebaseline clause (reduce reserved quantity by up to 20%) if the GPU cost index increases by >25% for 3 consecutive months. That clause must include a minimum notice period (30 days) and a right to cure (customer can choose to pay a temporary surcharge instead of reducing capacity).

3) Option C (escrow) — allowed only as a negotiated premium product; needs explicit approval from Exec and escrow design with Finance. Not default.

Next steps: Sean, prepare formal offer with Option B as the recommended path (balanced risk profile). Include clear formulas for the pass-through and the rebaseline trigger. Legal should draft the clause; I've looped Karthik for finance inputs.

Marissa
VP, Revenue — Redwood Inference

Term sheet (summary)
- Account: Integro AI | Deal ID: DEAL-INT-2028-045
- Offered constructs: Recommended = Option B (24m or 36m hybrid indexation with capped pass-through)

Option B (recommended)
- 24m base discount: 24% off list
- 36m base discount: 32% off list
- GPU market index pass-through: any monthly incremental GPU cost above a 15% baseline is shared; monthly pass-through capped at +10% of monthly committed bill.
- Rebaseline trigger: if GPU index > +25% vs baseline for 3 consecutive months, either party may request a rebaseline; customer may elect to pay a temporary surcharge (up to +15% on monthly committed bill) to avoid capacity reduction.

Exceptions & approvals
- We can offer up to 32% without Sr. Director sign-off; anything >32% triggers finance & Marissa sign-off. Escrow constructs and >38% discounts require VP/exec approval.
